title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
claim: Tokens that start spread over a sphere rapidly concentrate onto a low-dimensional set and stay there for moderate times.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right time snapshots, 3D spheres with orange curve overlay
description: Three 3D scatter plots on a wireframe unit sphere show the token distribution at times t=0, t=2.5 and t=5, labeled (a), (b) and (c) below each. In (a), about 2,000 semi-transparent points are spread over the whole sphere. The points are colored by position with a rainbow gradient: green on the left, blue at the bottom and center, purple and red on the right. A thin orange curve crosses the sphere. In (b) the points have collapsed into clusters strung along that orange curve. In (c) they form a few tight clusters along the orange circle, with green at one end and magenta/red at the other. Gray coordinate axes pass through the center of each sphere. The eye goes first to the colorful dense sphere on the left, then follows the collapse to the right.
caption: Illustration of Theorem [ref]. We observe concentration of $\rho_t^{\beta,n}$ at $E\cap \sphere$ (orange circle) when running [ref] with $n=2,000$ tokens to simulate [ref] for $B=R^\top\!\operatorname{diag}(5,5,1)R$ and $V=\mathrm{Id}$, where $R$ is a rotation by $\pi/8$. We use $\beta=\valbeta$ and a von Mises--Fisher mixture as initial density $\rho_0$.
abstract: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(Î²+1)}/Î²}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $Î²^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logÎ²$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $Î²$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.
